headline: Batting collapse: Bangladesh all out for 140 against Zimbabwe
summary: The Tigers struggled against pace and bounce at Harare Sports Club, recording their third-lowest Test innings ever against Zimbabwe.
details: Bangladesh suffered a severe batting collapse in their only Test match against Zimbabwe, being bowled out for just 140 runs in 47.2 overs.
After losing the toss and batting first at Harare Sports Club, the team struggled to handle the pace and bounce of the Zimbabwean bowlers.
Muminul Haque managed a half-century, but other key players failed to make a significant impact, with Sadman Islam scoring 20 and captain Najmul Hossain Shanto making 19.
The collapse was stark in the final stages, as Bangladesh lost seven wickets for the last 27 runs.
For Zimbabwe, Newman Nyamahuri was the standout performer, taking 4 wickets for 61 runs, while Ngaraava, Muzarabani, and Brad Evans each claimed two wickets.
This total marks Bangladesh's third-lowest innings in Test matches against Zimbabwe, with their lowest being 107 runs recorded 25 years ago.
Zimbabwe started their reply strongly, reaching 66 runs for no loss by the tea break.

headline_marked: Teesta River [[swells above danger level]] as upstream surge triggers red alert
headline: Teesta River swells above danger level as upstream surge triggers red alert
summary: Heavy rainfall and runoff from Bhutan and Sikkim have pushed water levels up, inundating cropland on riverine chars.
details: The Teesta River has risen above the danger mark following heavy rainfall and a fresh upstream surge, causing water to inundate cropland on riverine chars.
At the Dalia point in Nilphamari, the river was flowing at 52.22m on Sunday evening, which is 7cm above the danger level of 52.15m.
The surge was driven by runoff from the mountains of Bhutan and Sikkim, which also pushed the Teesta above danger levels at Domohani and Mekhliganj points in India's West Bengal.
Red alerts have been issued along the river in both Bangladesh and India to warn of potential flooding.
The Bangladesh Water Development Board has kept all 44 sluice gates of the Teesta Barrage open to manage the water flow.
Local administrations have advised residents in low-lying areas to remain vigilant and prepare for any emergency as authorities continue to monitor the situation.
caption:

Red alerts have been issued along the river in both Bangladesh and India to warn of potential flooding.

The Bangladesh Water Development Board has kept all 44 sluice gates of the Teesta Barrage open to manage the water flow.
